# EKO Perspectives project instructions

When working on any EKO Perspectives planning, research, post, profile or editorial task in this repository, first read `.editorial/EKO_EDITORIAL_WORKFLOW_v2.3.md`. When choosing article structure, also read `.editorial/story-engine-library.md`.

The repository's **EKO Editorial Workflow v2.3** is authoritative and supersedes v2.2 and the older separate `pre2015-prose-voice` and `ai-slop-editing-pass` workflow.

Do not draft a newly proposed topic until the owner has approved the topic/theme, unless the current request explicitly asks for that specific draft. Do not publish or modify published posts without explicit owner approval. New posts stay `draft: true`.

There is no single E360 formula and no fixed EKO article template. Choose a story engine after the evidence is understood. Check recent posts for repeated openings, caution moves, diagrams and endings. First person must refer to something the author actually did, observed, modelled, read, decided, experienced or believes. Where a claim is contested, read a strong credible rebuttal or competing interpretation. Public records can supply attributable voices, but never invent or imply reporting access that did not occur.

Preserve the workflow's evidence, story-engine, voice, final-edit, SEO/discovery, image, and rendered-page QA stages in their stated order. SEO is packaging, not a writing brief.

Every published post needs at least one relevant lead image stored locally with descriptive alt text and any required credit or licence. A second image is used only when it adds genuine explanatory, documentary or historical value; do not add decorative stock filler.
